drivingQuestion: Is the mishna redundant with the chapter's first mishna?
outcomeNote: The repetition teaches invalidity after the fact

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי? הָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ חֲדָא זִימְנָא – הַמֵּבִיא גֵּט מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם, צָרִיךְ שֶׁיֹּאמַר ״בְּפָנַי נִכְתַּב וּבְפָנַי נֶחְתַּם״! אִי מֵהַהִיא הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: צָרִיךְ, וְאִי לָא אָמַר כָּשֵׁר; קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» The Gemara asks with regard to the entire mishna: «Why do I» need all «these further» examples? «Didn’t it teach» these halakhot «once,» as the mishna states (2a): «One who brings a bill of divorce from a country overseas is required to say: It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence?» This indicates that if one did not state this declaration, then the bill of divorce is invalid. The Gemara explains: «If» the halakha were derived «from that» mishna alone, «I would say:» He is «required» to issue this statement ab initio, «but if he did not say» it the bill of divorce is nevertheless «valid» after the fact. Therefore, this mishna «teaches us» that the bill of divorce is invalid.
